presenter on Mass Save/energy summit; Building Design Committee member

public_comment.topic: Supports the boards making a decision on TCP and Brooks House rather than continuing to deliberate, having been involved in the master plan process; also relays a Mass Save presentation point that partial electrification across multiple buildings can outperform full electrification of one building.

budget_items.what_was_said: Facilities Director said putting a roof on the remaining, non-decommissioned part of TCP was estimated in winter and has likely gone up since.
A boiler that failed a required state inspection needs repair within 30 days or the state will begin fining the town.
Bringing the secondary boiler under control so it can be used costs money and would need to happen quickly once the primary fails.
Any renovation of TCP requires asbestos remediation regardless of scope, and the cost is expected to keep rising each year it's delayed.
A 2008 facilities list of needed repairs, never completed, was cited as totaling a large sum in today's dollars.
An earlier study to renovate the roughly 55,000 sq ft TCP building came back at a high cost, prompting a comparison to new construction.
A rough new-construction alternative on the same site, more space-efficient, was estimated higher due to pricing at the time.

budget_items.topic: Partial TCP roof repair (food pantry section only)
budget_items.what_was_said: An estimate to repair just enough roof to save the food-pantry/gym/bathroom section came in far higher than expected because the scope had to extend down the hallway.

budget_items.topic: FY23 capital plan hazardous abatement appropriation / TCP roof funding
budget_items.what_was_said: Town meeting appropriated funds in May 2022 for hazardous abatement at the old primary school; in November 2023 a portion was purportedly transferred to fund the TCP roof but the change was never reflected in MUNIS, leading to double-appropriated funds later corrected at this year's annual town meeting.
The town manager removed TCP operating costs from the operating budget and funded remaining TCP costs with one-time free cash for FY27 via a standalone article, which town meeting supported.
Before partial decommissioning, TCP's gas bill was cited as a major annual cost; after shutting half the building down, savings fell well short of the hoped-for reduction.

budget_items.topic: Mass Save Path 1 (net zero/low EUI) incentives
budget_items.what_was_said: Presenter described per-square-foot incentives for new construction/major renovation hitting low energy-use-intensity targets, plus a technical assistance and verification subsidy.

budget_items.topic: Mass Save Path 2 (whole-building energy use, up to 50,000 sq ft) incentives
budget_items.what_was_said: Incentives for buildings achieving a percentage energy reduction, plus cost-sharing for energy modeling and verification.

budget_items.topic: Mass Save Path 3 (high performance building) incentives
budget_items.what_was_said: Technical assistance funding is offered with a municipal cost-share requirement above a threshold, plus per-unit savings-based incentives.
figures_as_heard: 35 cents a kilowatt hour or $2 per therm

budget_items.what_was_said: Presenter listed per-ton incentive amounts for air source, variable refrigerant, and ground source heat pump systems.
National Grid is now sponsoring a shared or dedicated municipal energy manager position, covering wages for a period of years.
figures_as_heard: up to 120k a year for 3 years

budget_items.topic: Prior architecture/design spending (Taylor and Barnes, and a related study)
budget_items.what_was_said: Committee members recalled substantial prior spending on architecture and design studies across the TCP renovation study, TCP new-build study, and the failed Ritter redesign.

Facilities Director tasked with preparing cost estimates for TCP — either roof replacement costs if the building is kept, or asbestos abatement plus full demolition costs if it is not — to inform the FY28 capital plan discussion.
Select Board to schedule a tour of TCP, tentatively during the week of August 10th, pending full board being seated after the August 8th special election.
Select Board asked the Building Design Committee to bring back a formal recommendation/vote on the disposition of Brooks House.
Select Board asked the Building Design Committee to bring back a formal recommendation/vote on TCP.

Election voting equipment and polling location are being permanently relocated from TCP to the schools, with a mobile storage trailer serving as the permanent solution for voting equipment storage; town clerk is working with the state to finalize the change.
Next Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee meeting set for Monday, August 3rd at 5:30 p.m., location to be confirmed (possibly the planning office at Ritter or the library).

minutes.summary: A joint Select Board / Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee meeting opened with a presentation on Mass Save energy-summit incentives for building electrification, then shifted to a long workshop on the deteriorating TC Pacios (TCP) building — its failing systems, a history of a double-appropriated roof-repair fund later corrected at town meeting, and whether to repair or demolish it. No formal vote was taken on TCP or the Brooks House, but the group leaned toward not investing further in TCP, tasked the Facilities Director with cost estimates, and agreed the committee will bring formal recommendations on both buildings to a future meeting, with its next meeting set for August 3rd.
minutes.headline: Select Board leaned toward demolishing TC Pacios rather than repairing it, pending a formal committee vote.
